steps.text: Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk flour and garlic salt into butter until mixture is smooth. Slowly beat half and half into flour mixture until completely incorporated.
Whisk Parmesan cheese, parsley, and garlic into sauce; bring to a simmer. Cook and stir until sauce has thickened, 4 to 5 minutes. Use immediately or refrigerate.

raw_recipe.headline: Quick Alfredo Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This Alfredo sauce made with half-and-half is rich and creamy with less fat. It's quickly made on the stovetop in just 5 minutes and great over pasta.
raw_recipe.name: Quick Alfredo Sauce

review.reviewBody: I loved this. Added salt & pepper. Didn't have half & half so used 1-and-a-1/2 cups of milk and kept everything else the same. Great flavor and consistency.

Had some leftover half n half so I tried this. Pretty good. Be sure to cook the roux enough. Add the half n half slowly blending till smooth. Add the parma slowly and blend till smooth. I added just a splash of white wine. If this thickens too much just add a little extra water or half n half. I cooked some cleaned shrimp in the sauce till cooked through. Served over some brown rice with a garnish of parsley, fresh ground pepper and lemon slices.

I didn’t have half and half or parsley and a minimum amount of grated Parmesan cheese. I made my rue as usual 4 tbsp of butter and 4 tbsp of flour then substituted 2 cups of whole milk. Since I was lacking on the parm I added grated whole milk mozzarella and provolone. It did make the sauce a tad thicker so i ended up adding an extra 1/2 cup of milk to thin it out. Added a pulled rotisserie chicken and accompanied by bow tie pasta. 

**** add Cajun seasoning for a Cajun Alfredo pasta

After reading the reviews, and adhering to some of the advice, I give this recipe 5 stars because it's a great base that can be whipped up quickly and is easy to update......Spice can be added, not deleted, so there you have it. 

I agree, less flour is warranted. I used closer to 1/8 of a cup. Even so, I reserved some of the fettuccini water to thin as needed. Didn't need much.

Also, the parmesan definately needs increased for MY household's taste. If you have the green container (GC) parmesan, I would increase that to 1 cup, and I believe it would be excellent. But if you have block parmesan reggiano or pecorino, the flavor will travel a little further with less used. The GC varieties must have fillers to maintain long term preservation, but sacrifice some flavor. I used 1/3 cup GC parm and 1/3 cup mixed Parm reggiano and pecorino.

Finally, the spices......My husband and I love dynamic spice in everything, but not everyone does. We increased the minced garlic by twice, albeit jarred. And added lots of fresh ground pepper.

I used to make the traditional recipe years ago with heavy cream. Frankly, I like this one better with the minor adjustments.

This was UNREAL! I've made Alfredo Sauces before but none have been as good as this was. My additions: I minced up about 2T of onion and added an extra TBSP of butter to accommodate. Tossed the onion and the garlic in the butter and cooked until translucent and added about 1/4 cup of Italian cheese. I also used Fat Free half and half and an extra 1/2 cup of Fat Free Milk to thin the sauce since the extra cheese made it a little thick. Tossed in some cooked Penne noodles and topped with Garlic and herb marinated grilled chicken breast. A-freakin-mazing!

This was a pretty good, solid sauce that's perfect for anyone who's pressed on time. I was essentially looking for any recipe to use up my leftover half-and-half (which I had bought to make flan), and this did the trick nicely. I added a little fresh lemon juice and served it over fusille pasta with sauteed asparagus, shrimp, and a drizzle of chili garlic sauce for the spice.

I made a couple of substitutions, based on what I had in the house: whole milk instead of half-and-half, and garlic powder instead of garlic salt. Be sure to use "real" Parmesan cheese, not the flavorless canned stuff! (For speed, I shredded it in my food processor).

This sauce took me all of 8 minutes to prepare, including shredding the cheese, and has fabulous flavor that even my son, Mr. PickyPants, enjoyed! And it makes a LOT of sauce: I used it to rescue a big pot of chicken noodle soup no one was eating, which I'd made with 8 oz. of pasta and almost 2 lbs. of chicken. (I drained and froze the broth for later use.) Thanks so much for sharing the recipe!

I normally don't care for people who review a recipe, and then go on to talk about how they changed practically every ingredient - that is not the recipe then.
I am giving a heads-up to anyone looking for GLUTEN-FREE recipes. I made this recipe with 1 to 1 gluten-free flour (1 to 1 has xanthan gum added in the mix) and it worked GREAT! If you want a stronger flavour, add fresh cracked pink salt and peppercorns, and use more garlic and fresh parmesan. It also works well with full 35% cream.
This was so easy, and exactly what I was looking for. Thank you for the recipe. The quick preparation time is fantastic.
Once the sauce was done, I added thawed frozen cooked shrimp a couple of minutes before adding hot pasta.

I had only fat free half & half, decided to try it anyway. I used Locatelli Pecorino Romano, a bit of Parmesan, a little garlic powder for the garlic because I’m out of fresh... Loosened the sauce up a bit w/ some of the pasta water. TO DIE FOR!!!! Will definitely make again! Wow!

I used fat free half and half and lower fat Parmesan cheese. Also used frozen Normandy mixed vegetables thawed and heated in grill pan. Added left over grilled chicken. Also used Kamuta pasta. MY husband doesn’t eat vegetables, is diabetic and Italian. So this worked well.
Great and very filling meal.
Quick, easy and yummy. I sautéed the garlic lightly in the butter before adding only half of the the flour called for. I also added black pepper.
Family liked this a lot. I thought it was a little too thick. Next time I will adjust accordingly. Easy recipe.
Great Alfredo base. I used a hefty portion of Parmesan-Romano cheese, added a cup of frozen peas, some shredded chicken, and the secret ingredient: nutmeg.
It's a great recipe. Easy to follow and very delicious
I added cream cheese and left out the parsley. So creamy and delicious!
Very quick and simple. Used more parmesan -- grated plus shredded.
I followed the directions as directed only thing i changed is i use 1 1/2 cups of almond milk. Came out thick and very delicious. This is a keeper and I will be making it again!
was as good as I hoped ! ....added a frozen seafood assortment and the small amount of broth from cooking it . Keep stirring else film develops ! ... as good as advertised !!!!! .... Tim
Could use more Garlic, also salt pepper. Very light taste but okay
This was so easy and so full of flavor. I made it for fettuccini noodles and broccoli and it was great!
